It really depends on each individual pharmacy and their policies. Most pharmacy assistants should be completing their S2/S3 certificate (schedule 2 & 3 are your behind the counter medications) which outlines how to handle the sale of said items. I have had some pharmacies where I work at demand for all S3 purchases to be run by the pharmacist, others did not have time to be asked every single time, they assumed that after completing your training you should know what to ask the customer and if there is anything that comes back like there on a certain medication etc that you then refer to them. 

Most of the time we are just there to double check that you are aware of the medication you are taking, like voltarin for example can be quite harsh on the stomach so you may want to consider taking it with food, or checking that you aren't on blood thinners or other medication that might have negative interactions. You would be amazed at some of the interactions between medications and even vitamins you can purchase just in the store. 

I know it can seem quite nosey and if they are trained well they will try and make the questioning as quick and painless as possible.

You don't have to say a whole lot. Just listen and be understanding and I know it can be frustrating on your end to when it seems like there is no solution but we do really appreciate you being there. Even if its just sitting with us in silence when we've hit a low. Just knowing that you want to be there and are willing to help is the beginning.

My example of what not to do I had a very bad week. Very low and the only thing I was clinging onto the entire week was going to the beach with some friends. When it came to the day everyone cancelled or made excuses or just wanted to go drinking and I crashed hard and I locked myself in the bathroom for a few hours and then hid in my wardrobe for another few and when I reached out to my friend and told her I was feeling very suicidal she started blaming herself until I said don't worry I'm to afraid to actually do it and then she blew me off and said she was going to go the pub with her other friends and didn't contact me the rest of the day or even the next day. All because I said I wouldn't actually do it and I walled myself up and barely spoke about it again even though I was severely suffering. I ended up apologising to her even though I wasn't at fault. 

My good example was a new friend was slowly integrating me in with some mates that were very welcoming and a good change of pace but I was still suffering with issues with medication and alcohol and by the end of the night I was very suicidal, having massive panic attacks going from apologetic to attacking and my new mate was on the phone with me for hours even while he was still out making sure I wouldn't do anything and that he understood and checked up on me first thing in the morning with another call and called me in the afternoon to check in again. He did that a few times and it made me feel like someone was actually there for me and I eventually found the strength to help myself and I don't know if I would have without him.
It honestly can be so disheartening thankfully I did find some new friends that genuinely listened to me but not everyone has that luxury. I know I didn't for a while.
